units.title: Hands and Basic Cuts
units.blurb: The pinch grip, the claw, and the cuts every cook uses every day.

units.title: The Classic Cuts
units.blurb: The named cuts with their sizes, and the decorative cuts.

units.title: Keeping an Edge
units.blurb: Honing, sharpening and caring for knives.

topics.title: The Grip and the Guide Hand
topics.short: Pinch the blade where it meets the handle; curl the guide hand into a claw so the knuckles guide the flat of the blade and the fingertips stay tucked.
topics.trouble: Beginners hold the knife by the handle with a pointing finger on the spine, and flatten the guide hand with fingertips out.

topics.title: Slicing, Dicing an Onion and Mincing
topics.short: The rocking cut and the push cut; how to dice an onion with its root holding it together; mincing garlic and herbs.
topics.trouble: Cooks cut off the onion's root end first, so the layers fall apart before they can dice them.

topics.title: The Classic Cuts and Their Sizes
topics.short: Julienne, batonnet, brunoise and the small, medium and large dice have standard sizes, so food cooks evenly and looks deliberate.
topics.trouble: Learners mix up batonnet (¼ inch sticks) and julienne (⅛ inch sticks), or cut a dice that is really a pile of rough chunks.

topics.title: Chiffonade, Paysanne, Tourné and Other Shaped Cuts
topics.short: Ribbons of leaves, thin flat squares, rounds, bias and oblique cuts, and the seven-sided tourné.
topics.trouble: Cooks chiffonade basil with a dull knife and bruise it black, or roll leaves loosely so the ribbons are uneven.

topics.title: Honing and Sharpening
topics.short: Honing pushes a bent edge back into line; sharpening grinds new metal to make a new edge. Hold a steady angle, about 15 to 20 degrees per side.
topics.trouble: People think a steel sharpens; it only straightens. A knife that stays dull after honing needs a stone.

topics.title: Whetstones and Knife Care
topics.short: Coarse, medium and fine grits; raising and removing a burr; washing by hand, drying, storing in a block, strip or guard, and never leaving a knife in the sink.
topics.trouble: Cooks put good knives in the dishwasher or a drawer loose, and leave a knife under soapy water where someone can grab the blade.
